{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABism6fQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhMDOx8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 407, "title": "Switch macOS desktop voice typing to streaming clipboard paste", "body": "## Problem

The desktop voice-typing app now works for the user after #405 / PR #406, but macOS currently prefers Accessibility selected-text/range editing and falls back to synthetic Unicode keyboard events. The user wants **ordinary clipboard + native Paste as the primary text-insertion method**, while retaining streaming voice typing.

This is a product/implementation direction change, not a claim that the current app cannot input text. Clipboard paste is widely used by cross-application dictation tools and avoids relying on each application's Accessibility editing API or its handling of synthetic Unicode payloads. The current keyboard fallback also converts line breaks and tabs to spaces.

Current main: [92a3a29](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/commit/92a3a29e30e035f783215dae5b37933b9993e5b1).
- [desktop/mac-target.m](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/92a3a29e30e035f783215dae5b37933b9993e5b1/desktop/mac-target.m) selects direct AX edits or Unicode events.
- [desktop/session.js](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/92a3a29e30e035f783215dae5b37933b9993e5b1/desktop/session.js) already serializes output and handles Stop/Cancel.
- [docs/desktop.md](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/92a3a29e30e035f783215dae5b37933b9993e5b1/docs/desktop.md#focused-fields) describes the current insertion mechanism and limitations.

## Expected outcome

### 1. Standard clipboard paste, with streaming preserved

- Make clipboard + native Cmd+V the **default macOS desktop text-insertion path**, not merely a hidden fallback behind Accessibility editing. Simplify or remove superseded direct-edit/Unicode-dispatch code and tests where no longer needed. Do not add a new user-facing insertion-mode selector or per-app configuration for this change.
- Keep the current generic Focused Application Text Output node, graph schema, Pipeline and committed TEXT delivery semantics. Each nonempty committed chunk should be pasted promptly during recording, without waiting for Stop or accumulating the entire transcript. Never insert provisional hypotheses. Identical committed chunks are separate deliveries, not duplicates to deduplicate.
- Reuse the existing serialized output queue. For each chunk, temporarily stage its text in the clipboard, dispatch the normal native Paste shortcut, allow the target a practical opportunity to consume the clipboard, and restore the previous clipboard when safe before proceeding to the next chunk. Preserve Unicode, Japanese, emoji, whitespace, newlines and tabs as clipboard text; allow the target application's usual paste behavior, including selection replacement, formatting, truncation or rejection.
- Use a conventional native mechanism with normal OS permissions (e.g. NSPasteboard/Electron clipboard and CGEvent for Cmd+V). Choose a small implementation based on actual reference code and available APIs; no browser extension, DOM bridge, new resident service or custom browser.
- macOS is the required target for this change. Keep the clipboard transaction and queue design reusable for Linux X11 / other desktop hosts where practical, but do not require porting those platforms in this Issue. Preserve the existing X11 behavior and keep its current limitations explicit; do not claim Linux has switched if it has not. Web/extension/Playground behavior remains independent and unchanged.

### 2. Practical clipboard management and native safety

Use established clipboard-paste techniques rather than inventing a complex universal editing system.

- Serialize paste transactions so rapid committed chunks cannot overwrite one another's clipboard payload before the receiving app has a reasonable opportunity to paste. Use an appropriate bounded consumption signal or settling interval based on the selected technique. Do not treat a clipboard read or a dispatched key event as definitive proof that the intended app completed its paste. No universal paste acknowledgement, atomic external edit, or perfect timing guarantee is required.
- Snapshot/restore existing clipboard items and formats where practical, not just plain text. Use pasteboard ownership/generation (e.g. macOS changeCount) or equivalent guards. If a user/other application changes the clipboard during the transaction, do not restore an old snapshot over the new contents. Handle clipboard write failure, cancellation, and cleanup without blindly repeating a possibly delivered paste. Do not retain or log the user's clipboard or dictated text unnecessarily. Document unavoidable clipboard-history/clipboard-manager effects and timing limitations.
- Keep the practical safeguards established in #401, #403 and #405: explicit user Start, ordinary OS authorization, available application/window/field identity checks before dispatch, stop on observed target change, cancel pending output, prevent app-caused duplicate dispatch, and refuse known secure/password/read-only targets where identifiable. Wait for held shortcut modifiers to release; do not generate Enter/Submit or other unrelated commands. Missing or incomplete Accessibility editing metadata alone is **not** a reason to refuse paste.
- Do not reintroduce application, bundle-ID, role, toolkit or test-target allowlists, warnings for untested apps, or an unnecessary confirmation dialog. Do not require exact read-back of an edit, all-or-nothing insertion, or complete elimination of the previously accepted OS-level in-flight focus race. Stop drains accepted queued chunks subject to normal target checks; Cancel/Quit discard pending output, allow safe cleanup of an in-flight clipboard transaction, and prevent subsequent dispatch.
- Keep the fix proportional. Do not turn clipboard timing or third-party application behavior into an open-ended compatibility investigation or require an elaborate settings UI. Ordinary target-side constraints and the residual risks inherent in native paste are acceptable, documented limitations.

### 3. Reference implementations

Before implementing, inspect the relevant actual source at identifiable revisions, reusing proven techniques where appropriate and respecting licenses. Existing investigation in [docs/evidence/desktop-401.md](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/evidence/desktop-401.md#insertion-decision) already documents clipboard generation guards, early restoration problems and platform tradeoffs.

- [Handy](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy): [clipboard.rs](https://github.com/cjpais/Handy/blob/main/src-tauri/src/clipboard.rs), native paste and restoration/serialization techniques.
- [OpenWhispr](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr): [clipboard.js](https://github.com/OpenWhispr/openwhispr/blob/main/src/helpers/clipboard.js), especially relevant because it also uses Electron.
- [Vocalinux](https://github.com/VocaHQ/vocalinux): [text injection implementation](https://github.com/VocaHQ/vocalinux/blob/main/src/vocalinux/text_injection/text_injector.py) and clipboard restoration tests; relevant to sequential dictation and Linux.
- [GladiaFlow](https://github.com/gladiaio/gladiaflow) and [WindVoice](https://github.com/mackatwentytsuru/windvoice): investigate as candidate streaming/utterance-by-utterance insertion references. Their public descriptions were reviewed in the initial discussion; the exact transaction implementations have not yet been independently verified. Do not assume they solve all clipboard races.
- [Apple NSPasteboard](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appkit/nspasteboard), [Electron clipboard](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/clipboard), [Apple CGEvent](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/coregraphics/cgevent).

Use the relevant references, briefly explain the selected approach in the PR, and avoid making exhaustive comparative research a separate completion gate.

### Pre-merge acceptance (automated; no human gate)

- [ ] The normal macOS external text output uses native clipboard paste, including when direct Accessibility editing is unavailable. It does not wait for recording to end. Existing graph and output contracts remain unchanged.
- [ ] Deterministic tests at the lightest useful layer exercise multiple rapid committed deliveries (including equal text, Japanese, emoji and multiline text) during an active session. Each chunk is staged and dispatched once, in order; simulated delayed paste consumption does not read the next chunk or a prematurely restored clipboard in the tested timing model. Provisional output is not pasted.
- [ ] Tests exercise normal restoration, representative non-text clipboard formats where the API supports them, intervening user copy/ownership changes, error and cancellation cleanup, held modifiers and observed target change. No new dispatch after cancellation, no blind retry of ambiguous paste, no overwriting a newer clipboard, and no automatic submit. Keep these tests representative rather than requiring all formats, apps or possible OS scheduling scenarios.
- [ ] Build and launch the macOS package and run `npm test` and applicable focused desktop regression tests. Preserve existing permission-independent coverage. Use a representative editor/browser or controlled host fixture to test paste behavior; actual independent external-app tests that require unavailable OS Accessibility/keyboard-event authorization remain optional, as agreed in #401. Report them as unverified if unavailable. Do not ask the user to grant permissions or perform manual confirmation as a merge/closure condition. No new real-model download or exhaustive compatibility matrix is necessary for a text-output-only change.
- [ ] Update the desktop guide and PR description with clipboard behavior, streaming semantics, practical limitations and concise optional manual test steps: prepare the model, focus an ordinary editor or browser field, start dictation, observe successive chunks arriving before Stop, stop, and check clipboard preservation. Include relevant build/launch instructions and permissions. Do not limit production use to the representative test apps. Record actual results and run `git diff --check`.

## Required post-merge verification

None. User testing and permission-dependent native checks remain optional and must not keep this Issue open. Actual subsequently observed defects should be tracked separately.

## Context

Follow-up to #401, #403 and #405 / merged PRs #402, #404 and #406. The user explicitly requested switching to the clipboard method without losing real-time incremental input. Follow the repository's [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md), and README UI/UX principles.
